parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Section three.

You will hear two industrial design students called John and Debbie discussing research for a presentation on a new building.

First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-six on page five.

Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-six.

Hi, John.

Hi, Debbie. Should we get ready for our presentation?

Yes. Well, we have to give a presentation to our seminar group about Education House, the new government building that uses cooling, heating, and water in an environmentally friendly way.

Let's start with a diagram of the building so the other students can see what it looks like.

Well, here's a very simplified diagram with symbols to represent key areas of the design.

Shall we look at it and see if we can explain the different processes?

Yes. Firstly, on the left-hand side of the roof, there's a cooling tower.

Yes. This is where hot, stale air from inside the building rises naturally up a chimney. Uh, there are exhaust fans mounted on the roof that push the air out.

Okay. Moving along the top of the roof to the right-hand side, we have the weather station. This monitors how cool the outside air is. Once this is assessed, then the information is fed to computers, and these activate the necessary heating or cooling processes.

Okay. Let's talk now about the cooling processes.

On the right-hand side of the building below the timber shutters is the part they call the shower tower.

This is where water falls through a three-story tube, sucking in air from outside as it falls. The unusual thing about it is this fresh air actually helps to cool the building.

Yes. It's amazing, really. Okay, below ground level in the basement on the right-hand side is a tank, which forms another part of the cooling process. The tank is full of small metal balls. Water passes through this tank. Each time it does this, the balls absorb the heat from the water, making it cooler without using any energy.

What should we talk about next?

Well, you see the balcony below the light shelf.

What happens there?

Rainwater is fed down from the roof, and this is where it's used to water the plants that cover the outside wall.

What about the square above the light shelf? It represents a window, doesn't it?

Yes. That's important to point out. Because the upper floor windows get more daylight than the lower floor ones, the windows at the top of the building are smaller than those at the bottom. This means energy is saved higher up in the building because not as much heat is wasted through large windows.

Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-seven to thirty on page six.

Now listen and answer questions twenty-seven to thirty.

Let's continue the presentation by giving our opinions on some of the features of the building. Let's talk about what we thought was surprising about the building.

Yes. It's not out of the ordinary in terms of size. I mean, it's well under the height of the surrounding buildings. Also, in the past, I think people would have been surprised by the vegetation on the facades, but that's become quite common now.

That's right. But we both agreed that the access to the building through a shopping arcade is quite unusual.

Yes. The way in is behind a small cafe, which is not what you'd expect. Now, should we mention the findings on staff productivity in the building? According to one article, the access to greenery and vegetation is increasing productivity by relieving stress.

Yes, I remember that article.

Researchers have been monitoring this for a couple of years now, so the results are clear. But to be honest, I think it's pretty obvious that you feel calmer seeing greenery around you.

Yes. We've been reading that in newspapers for ages, haven't we? So I wouldn't bother to mention it.

Okay. So we haven't mentioned the edge space yet. You know, the place that's been marked for social interaction between workers, where you can have a coffee and a chat. What are your thoughts about it?

Well, I'm just amazed the management allowed it. I'm sure all the staff love to get away from their desks. I would. I'm just not sure how much work I'd get done if I had an edge space to go to.

[chuckles] I agree. Okay, let's think about the water system now. They want to supply one hundred percent of their own non-drinking water needs by recycling water, and it looks like they are on target to complete this stage of the project by early next year. But, you know, I don't think the staff are gonna respond well to this.

I agree. People just don't like using too much recycled water, even though it's been proven to pose no health risks whatsoever.

Well, I've really enjoyed researching this building.

That is the end of section three. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

analyses.content: 录音提到在这个冷却塔里，室内陈旧的热空气会上升并通过排风扇被推出去，对应选项F“旧空气被移除”。
你可能会被“hot”误导去选跟温度相关的选项，但这里的核心动作是“push the air out（把空气推出去）”。

Firstly, on the left-hand side of the roof, there's a cooling tower. Yes. This is where hot, stale air from inside the building rises naturally up a chimney. Uh, there are exhaust fans mounted on the roof that push the air out.
录音指出气象站的作用是监测外面空气有多凉，对应选项G“检查温度”。
你可能会听到“fed to computers”或“heating or cooling processes”而想得太多，但气象站最基础的功能只是“monitors how cool（监测有多凉）”。

Moving along the top of the roof to the right-hand side, we have the weather station. This monitors how cool the outside air is. Once this is assessed, then the information is fed to computers, and these activate the necessary heating or cooling processes.
录音讲到这里的水落下时会从外面吸入空气（sucking in air from outside），这就对应了选项B“吸入新鲜空气”。
你可能会听到“water falls”就立刻去找关于水的选项，但紧接着的“sucking in air”才是这个淋雨塔带来的独特作用。

On the right-hand side of the building, below the timber shutters, is the part they call the shower tower. This is where water falls through a three-story tube, sucking in air from outside as it falls. The unusual thing about it is this fresh air actually helps to cool the building.
录音明确说明金属球会吸收水里的热量，让水变得更凉（making it cooler），对应选项H“降低水温”。
你可能会因为听到“tank is full of small metal balls”而忽略了后面真正的动作结论是“making it cooler（让水变凉）”。

Okay, below ground level, in the basement on the right-hand side, is a tank, which forms another part of the cooling process. The tank is full of small metal balls. Water passes through this tank. Each time it does this, the balls absorb the heat from the water, making it cooler without using any energy.
录音提到雨水从屋顶流下，在这里被用来浇灌外墙上的植物（used to water the plants），对应选项E“使用雨水”。
你可能会只听到“rainwater is fed down”就去选带rainwater的其他干扰项，但重点是它被“used（使用）”来浇花了。
Well, you see the balcony below the light shelf. What happens there? Rainwater is fed down from the roof, and this is where it's used to water the plants that cover the outside wall.
录音解释说顶层窗户较小，这样就不会有太多的热量通过大窗户浪费掉（not as much heat is wasted），对应选项C“减少热量流失”。
你可能会被“energy is saved”误导去自己猜测别的选项，但紧跟着的“heat is wasted”直接对应了“heat loss”。

What about the square above the light shelf? It represents a window, doesn't it? Yes. That's important to point out. Because the upper floor windows get more daylight than the lower floor ones, the windows at the top of the building are smaller than those at the bottom. This means energy is saved higher up in the building because not as much heat is wasted through large windows.

你可能听到“height”或“vegetation on the facades”就想选A或C，但录音明确否定了这两点，说它们“not out of the ordinary（没什么特别的）”和“become quite common now（现在很常见了）”。

Let's talk about what we thought was surprising about the building. Yes. It's not out of the ordinary in terms of size. I mean, it's well under the height of the surrounding buildings. Also, in the past, I think people would have been surprised by the vegetation on the facades, but that's become quite common now. That's right. But we both agreed that the access to the building through a shopping arcade is quite unusual. Yes. The way in is behind a small cafe, which is not what you'd expect.

questions.question: What do they think about the' edge space' in the building?

录音里提到了员工肯定喜欢离开办公桌去那里，你如果不注意听可能会主观臆断这会导致工作效率下降从而不受欢迎（A选项），同时千万别漏掉说话人表达态度的核心情感词“amazed”。

Okay. So we haven't mentioned the edge space yet. You know, the place that's been marked for social interaction between workers, where you can have a coffee and a chat. I'm just not sure how much work I'd get done if I had an edge space to go to.

你可能会听到“health risks”去选C，但录音说的是“pose no health risks（没有健康风险）”，直接排除了C项干扰。

Okay, let's think about the water system now. They want to supply one hundred percent of their own non-drinking water needs by recycling water, and it looks like they are on target to complete this stage of the project by early next year.
